content: 1. The combination of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of tinidazole by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction necessitates close monitoring and potential therapy modification. 2. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may lead to elevated plasma concentrations associated with serious or life-threatening events. Examples include tipranavir and the combination of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF. 3. Tipranavir can increase the levels or effects of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 4. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Tisotumab vedotin’s active metabolite, MMAE, is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE, raising the risk of adverse effects. Close monitoring is required. 5. The combination of tobramycin and elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF, when coadministered with tolmetin, can increase the toxicity of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Co-administration of emtricitabine and tenofovir with other drugs primarily excreted by glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, such as high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs, may result in toxicity. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and close monitoring is necessary. 8. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat, as a CYP2D6 inhibitor, necessitates caution with CYP2D6 substrates that may lead to elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 9. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 10. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can decrease the levels of torsemide by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. 11. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat, as a CYP2D6 inhibitor, necessitates caution with CYP2D6 substrates that may lead to elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 12. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 13. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat, as a CYP3A4 inhibitor, may require benzodiazepine dose reduction. 15. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decrease its levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. 16. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat, as a CYP2D6 inhibitor, necessitates caution with CYP2D6 substrates that may lead to elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 17. Ublituximab may decrease the effects of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 18. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 19. Valacyclovir and elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase each other’s toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 20. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The valbenazine dose should be reduced to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Valganciclovir and elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase each other’s toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 22. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vamorolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The starting dose of vamorolone should be reduced to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if weight >50 kg. 23. Vancomycin and elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A dose of 5 mg in 72 hours is recommended. 25. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat, as a CYP2D6 inhibitor, necessitates caution with CYP2D6 substrates that may lead to elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 26. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 27. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 28. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 29. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 30. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 31. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, and alternative drugs should be considered. 32. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 33. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, and alternative drugs should be considered. 35. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Both cobicistat and voriconazole are CYP3A4 inhibitors, and the benefit/risk ratio should be assessed to justify coadministration. 36. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can decrease the levels of zafirlukast by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. 37. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The zanubrutinib dose should be reduced to 80 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Dose interruption may be required for adverse reactions, and the previous dose should be resumed after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 38. Zidovudine is contraindicated with elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF. This combination should not be administered with other antiretrovirals, as elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF constitute a complete regimen for HIV. 39. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 40. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations and serious or life-threatening events. 41. Elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The zuranolone dose should be reduced when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 42. Common adverse effects of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF include proteinuria (39%), nausea (16%), diarrhea (12%), abnormal dreams (9%), headache (7%), increased serum creatinine (7%), fatigue (5%), increased creatine kinase ≥10x ULN (5%), increased serum lipids (4%), rash (3%), dizziness (3%), insomnia (3%), hematuria (3%), flatulence (2%), increased AST >5x ULN (2%), increased amylase >2x ULN (2%), somnolence (1%), and ocular icterus. Immune system disorders include allergic reactions such as angioedema. Metabolic disorders include lactic acidosis, hypokalemia, and hypophosphatemia. Respiratory disorders include dyspnea. Gastrointestinal disorders include pancreatitis, increased amylase, and abdominal pain. Hepatobiliary disorders include hepatic steatosis, hepatitis, and increased liver enzymes (commonly AST, ALT, gamma GT). Skin disorders include rash. Musculoskeletal disorders include rhabdomyolysis, osteomalacia (manifested as bone pain and potential fractures), muscular weakness, and myopathy. Renal disorders include acute renal failure, renal failure, acute tubular necrosis, Fanconi syndrome, proximal renal tubulopathy, interstitial nephritis (including acute cases), nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and renal insufficiency.
